records.title: Contain derived and query-shape disclosure
records.body:
## Parent

#4 — Protect MCP fields with mask-token round trips

## What to build

Prevent indirect disclosure by propagating protection through derived fields and by rejecting queries whose result membership, ordering, grouping, or counts depend on protected information.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Protection provenance propagates transitively through formulas, lookups, rollups, and linked-row display labels.
- [ ] Direct and derived protected data is masked at the smallest semantic leaf while proven-public identifiers and ordering remain usable.
- [ ] Display-only derivative tokens cannot be redeemed in row mutations.
- [ ] Searches, filters, sorts, groups, membership tests, and counts that depend on protected provenance are rejected before the underlying query executes.
- [ ] Unknown contracts, unsupported output shapes, broken dependencies, and unprovable provenance fail closed for non-empty policies.
- [ ] Every registered MCP tool declares its protected inputs, outputs, and operation class.
- [ ] Tests cover multi-level dependencies, linked labels, cycles, broken references, unknown field adapters, safe public structure, and pre-query rejection.

## Blocked by

- #7 — Create an endpoint that masks direct protected fields

records.title: Productionize ConvRot and stage incremental Diffusers memory optimizations
records.body:
## Goal

Turn the `convrot-optimization` research checkpoint into maintainable, model-neutral ConvRot operators first, then adopt only the narrow Diffusers memory-fusion seams that do not require transformer-block replacement.

Research source:

- Branch: [`convrot-optimization`](https://github.com/Boffee/piper-kernels/tree/convrot-optimization)
- Core checkpoint: [`b0817bd`](https://github.com/Boffee/piper-kernels/commit/b0817bd1a80a690486ff742f2a8b86d955ce7fcc)
- Organized research checkpoint: [`f9fd9df`](https://github.com/Boffee/piper-kernels/commit/f9fd9df252a3d3ce81bc2066bad17f30ac70c9b3)
- Core report: [`docs/convrot-optimization.md`](https://github.com/Boffee/piper-kernels/blob/convrot-optimization/docs/convrot-optimization.md)
- Follow-on report: [`docs/convrot-follow-on-experiments.md`](https://github.com/Boffee/piper-kernels/blob/convrot-optimization/docs/convrot-follow-on-experiments.md)
- Adoption roadmap: [`docs/convrot-adoption.md`](https://github.com/Boffee/piper-kernels/blob/convrot-optimization/docs/convrot-adoption.md)

The branch is a research record, not a merge candidate. Every child should land through focused PRs against `main`.

## Priority and tracking

### P0 — standalone ConvRot

- [ ] #26 — productize the benchmark/operator contract, factorized one-pass preparation, 64-bit addressing, and explicit input-SwiGLU API
- [ ] #27 — integrate the architecture-gated large-M INT8 GEMM schedule and retain portable scheduling

Stopping after P0 is valid: the standalone operator already provides the principal ConvRot speed and weight/activation-memory benefits without any model-block replacement.

### P1 — straightforward Diffusers adoption

- [ ] [Boffee/piper#94](https://github.com/Boffee/piper/issues/94) — add reversible MiniMax-H3 linear conversion and the localized input-SwiGLU feed-forward seam

Piper Kernels remains model-neutral. Piper owns model discovery, checkpoint conversion, offload, LoRA, hooks, integration order, and real-model validation.

### P2 — first local memory-fusion boundary

- [ ] #28 — add the model-neutral fused QKV + Q/K RMSNorm + partial-RoPE operator
- [ ] [Boffee/piper#95](https://github.com/Boffee/piper/issues/95) — install it through the MiniMax-H3 attention processor while preserving the selected attention backend

This is intentionally the first post-ConvRot fusion because the current processor already owns the complete local boundary. It does not require replacing `MiniMaxH3TransformerBlock`.

## Dependency order

```text
#26 standalone operator / exact preparation / input-SwiGLU
 ├── #27 architecture-gated GEMM scheduling
 └── Boffee/piper#94 reversible Diffusers linear + feed-forward conversion

#26 + #27
 └── #28 fused QKV RMSNorm/partial-RoPE operator

Boffee/piper#94 + #28
 └── Boffee/piper#95 MiniMax-H3 attention-processor integration
```

The Diffusers converter may be developed once #26 is stable, but full performance acceptance uses both #26 and #27.

## Deferred findings — do not open implementation issues yet

Keep these documented here until their readiness conditions are met:

- **Segmented scale/shift into ConvRot preparation:** the lower-risk precursor to RMSNorm/AdaLN fusion because it retains the existing RMSNorm output and numerical contract.
- **Full RMSNorm/AdaLN preparation:** blocked on selecting and quality-testing a reduction/numerical contract; the prototype differed from eager PyTorch by up to two INT8 codes and 0.77% row-scale relative error.
- **Gated-residual GEMM epilogue:** blocked on a functional/mutating alias contract, version-counter behavior, reusable segment mapping, and shape-specific liveness tuning; the short-sequence FC2 gain was marginal.
- **Paired FC1 output-SwiGLU:** an alternative to input-SwiGLU rather than an additive optimization; promote only if the approximately 3% isolated chain gain survives real-model validation.
- **Combined MiniMax-H3 block wrapper:** consider only after the independent operators and narrow adapters pass real-model quality, offload, hooks, compile, and memory tests.
- **Production `triton_op` migration:** integration cleanup for trace/export visibility, not a speed issue and not a prerequisite unless a later consumer requires it.
- **SM89/other-architecture tuning:** create one family-specific issue after SM120 lands; never generalize SM120 schedules without measurement.

## Design rules for future composition

- Core operators remain independent of Diffusers, ComfyUI, checkpoint formats, and offload policy.
- Every fused boundary has an explicit tensor-level API, declared logical-dtype semantics, portable materialized fallback, and architecture/shape guard.
- Adapters use independent feature flags instead of one all-or-nothing fused-block switch.
- Packed tensors remain registered on modules, with canonical storage shared by ordinary and fused paths.
- Model conversion is reversible and reports enabled features and skip reasons.
- Reused original child modules retain their identity. An eliminated standalone operation cannot fire its original forward hook; expose a hookable fused boundary or select fallback.
- Unsupported shape, training, active incompatible LoRA, semantic hooks, or unsupported offload state selects the original materialized path.
- Do not add isolated microbenchmark speedups together and report them as model-level improvement.

## Cross-cutting acceptance criteria

- Every kernel-changing PR records correctness, output quality, device and complete-operator latency, registers, spills, shared memory, tested GPU, power limit, and software versions.
- Benchmarks distinguish preparation, prepared GEMM, complete operation, and model-level timing.
- 37,710-row and 131,072-row coverage includes rows around relevant signed-32-bit element-offset boundaries.
- Every promoted composite covers eager, fake/meta, `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)`, export where applicable, dynamic rows, optimized and fallback paths.
- Diffusers integration validates one real block

records.title: [MASTER][TestPyPI] QuReddy standalone 10/10 release-candidate program
records.body:
## Master roadmap — QuReddy 10/10 release-candidate program

This is the single canonical roadmap tracker for base QuReddy (`breachsafe/qureddy`,
Apache-2.0, 0.2.x). All in-flight work has been consolidated here as a categorized checklist
so the board stays actionable. Each checkbox links its source issue; folded issues are closed
and point back here. Reopen an individual issue only if it needs standalone tracking.

Kept open standalone alongside this tracker: **#92** (OpenSSF Best Practices badge — active
goal), **#201** and **#202** (live correctness bugs). Everything else lives in the checklist
below.

## Decision

Make public `breachsafe/qureddy` the sole product and release authority and take the
standalone package to a verified TestPyPI release candidate before any Qurum, TAO, Prowler
or Enterprise integration work.

Distribution contract:

```text
pipx install breachsafe-qureddy
  -> qureddy runs on supported Python/OS combinations
  -> SSH works without OpenSSL
  -> TLS uses an explicitly supported external OpenSSL
  -> JSON is parseable and contract-stable
  -> CycloneDX 1.7 CBOM is honest and independently valid
  -> failures preserve UNKNOWN/NOT_TESTABLE and correct exit codes
  -> artifacts trace to protected public source with attestations
```

## Consolidated work checklist

### Correctness bugs
- [ ] SLH-DSA certs mis-classified as NOT post-quantum — FIPS 205 missing from the PQC table (#201) — *open standalone*
- [ ] Evidence excerpt not derived from the stream its sha256 attests — integrity mismatch (#202) — *open standalone*
- [ ] Reproducible CBOM mode hashes host-specific executable paths (#207)

### Testing hardening
- [ ] Recapture all OpenSSL fixtures/goldens on 3.5.7 LTS (#104)
- [ ] Raise coverage floor 86% → 90% and cover the 5 named untested error/crypto modules (#109)
- [ ] Adopt property-based testing (Hypothesis) — would have caught #116/#128/#130 (#131)
- [ ] Add fuzzing coverage for TLS/SSH parsers (OSS-Fuzz or ClusterFuzzLite) (#86)
- [ ] Prove reproducible CBOM output across Python hash seeds (#196)

### CI + OpenSSF badge
- [ ] Earn the OpenSSF Best Practices passing badge (CII-Best-Practices = 0) (#92) — *open standalone*
- [ ] OpenSSF Scorecard hardening: 6.1 → 8+ (#88)
- [ ] Badge criteria audit follow-through: 1 falsely-Met → N/A, 16 undermarked, 2 sections not exported (#217)
- [ ] `report_responses`: establish and evidence maintainer responses to reports (passing MUST) (#218)
- [ ] Enable branch protection on main requiring approved review (#84)
- [ ] Pin every supported platform to OpenSSL 3.5.7 LTS in CI (#70)
- [ ] Sign all release artifacts (Scorecard Signed-Releases) (#219)
- [ ] Ensure every merged PR runs CI checks (Scorecard CI-Tests) (#220)
- [ ] Hash-pin the Dockerfile pip install (Scorecard Pinned-Dependencies) (#221)
- [ ] Run CodeQL on push, not just PRs/schedule (Scorecard SAST) (#222)

### Features
- [ ] Output ergonomics: compact JSON, `--output FILE`, severity filter (#133)
- [ ] SSH scanner depth vs ssh-audit; CBOM currently drops host keys (#143)
- [ ] Classify signature algorithms in `algorithmProperties` (#177)
- [ ] Optional web UI via breachsafe-wizard (`[ui]` extra + `qureddy ui`, Docker backend) (#181)

### Governance / ADRs
- [ ] Lineage ADR: canonical engine trunk + Pro UX shell, one-way merge, drift-gated (#204)
- [ ] Single-source identity (version/branding/edition) via config + generation (#205)
- [ ] Version/identity inconsistencies: stale Dockerfile ARG, doc banners, bump_version.py gaps (#206)
- [ ] CI/CD audit follow-ups (PR #96, duplicate-repo note) (#111)

### CBOM
- [ ] Emit correlated JSON + CBOM from one scan (#187)
- [ ] CBOM emission target for MVP 0.3 — CycloneDX 1.7 profile / Cryptography Registry (#200)
- [ ] Optionally emit `breachsafe:v1:*` OSCAL-observation properties in CBOM output (#180)

## Ordered execution

Do not parallelize load-bearing changes across the same files. Sequence is:

1. #30 — restore truthful green product structure and machine-output contracts.
2. #31 — implement the honest CycloneDX 1.7 observation contract.
3. #32 — independently prove final-byte CycloneDX conformance.
4. #33 — prove clean pip/pipx installation and dependency reproducibility.
5. #34 — make one local-first release gate fail closed; hosted CI only mirrors it.
6. #35 — true up first-user, reference and release documentation.
7. #36 — run a manual, scoped-token TestPyPI rehearsal and verify the indexed artifact.

## Stop-the-line rules

- Do not publish any TestPyPI artifact until the local release evidence gate passes.
- Do not call CBOM 1.7 complete on serializer output alone.
- Do not bundle or imply pip installs OpenSSL.
- Do not suppress dependency/security findings without a narrow, dated, owned exception.
- Do not let live Internet tests make ordinary PRs flaky; hermetic proofs block, live probes
  run separately.
- Do not add Qurum/TAO/Prowler work to this milestone.
- Do not publish to production PyPI under this issue.

## TestPyPI exit gate

- all #30-#35 acceptance gates closed;
- clean public source commit and documented review;
- clean Git checkout;
- local fail-closed release gate green with exact command evidence;
- CycloneDX 1.7 final bytes independently valid;
- wheel/sdist built once, inspected and clean-installed;
- accurate PyPI-rendered docs;
- manual TestPyPI upload with a project-scoped token and human approval;
- artifact digest, source commit and evidence-manifest digest recorded;
- clean install from TestPyPI proves the public user path.

Only then hold a separate go/no-go for production PyPI. Production remains blocked until an
available supported OIDC Trusted Publisher can provide PyPI attestations.

records.title: Topological sort silently produces an incomplete order for cyclic graphs (not currently reachable, but a latent correctness gap)
records.body:
## Found via
Writing #5's test suite made me think about what \`topologicalSortSteps\` does on a graph with a cycle, since Kahn's algorithm (which it implements) is only defined for DAGs.

## Bug
\`topologicalSortSteps\` (src/visualizers/graph/steps/topological.ts) never checks whether every node was actually dequeued. If the input graph has a cycle, the nodes in that cycle keep a non-zero in-degree forever and are never enqueued/visited - the algorithm just stops with a queue that permanently empties out early. \`useGraphDerivedState\`'s \`deriveTopoOrder()\` builds the "Topological Order" output purely from \`mark-visited\` steps, so the output panel would silently show an order with only some of the nodes - no error, no cycle indicator, and \`order.length < graph.nodes.length\` is never checked anywhere.

## Why this isn't urgent
Not currently reachable: the graph visualizer only offers fixed presets (\`GRAPH_PRESETS\`, no user-editable graph), and the \`dependency\` preset used for Topological Sort is a genuine DAG. So no user can trigger this today.

## Fix (when it matters)
Worth guarding before any future work makes the graph user-editable (a custom-graph input, an example picker with more presets, etc.): after the main loop, compare how many nodes got \`mark-visited\` against \`graph.nodes.length\`, and either push a distinct \`cycle-detected\`-style step or otherwise surface that the order is incomplete, rather than silently truncating it. Also worth adding a cyclic-graph test case to #5's topological-sort tests once that guard exists.

records.title: RFC: minimal immutable prefix checkpoint tree for Flash KV reuse
records.body:
# RFC: Minimal immutable prefix checkpoint tree for Flash KV reuse

## Status

Revision 5 after terminal-boundary, atomic-lifecycle, and eviction-policy clarification.

**Recommendation: conditional Go**, delivered as three independently gated slices:

1. **P0a — engine proof:** exact split/capture/restore, no server lookup and no durable cache.
2. **P0b — RAM-only token-text tree:** usable prefix reuse under a hard global memory budget.
3. **P0c — immutable disk persistence:** FIFO writer, restart scan, shared disk budget, and leaf-only GC.

The proposed object remains one narrow immutable **prefix tree**, not a generic DAG, radix database, paged-KV system, or new protocol state machine. Every node has exactly one parent and contains:

- the compressed/indexer rows added since that parent; and
- the exact terminal frontier required to continue inference at this node.

KVC v1 remains the fallback and correctness oracle until P0c has passed the full matrix.

Revision 5 makes three operational rules explicit:

1. every real prompt terminal is an exact, variable-length capture candidate, even when it is only a few tokens after its parent;
2. a node's history delta and terminal frontier have one atomic publication, persistence, and deletion lifecycle in P0;
3. RAM-only pruning and durable deletion are leaf-only; RAM payload offload may target an internal node only when a durable copy remains available.

## Why a tree is sufficient

Given cached branches:

```text
[SYSTEM][A][B][C]
[SYSTEM][A][B][D]
[SYSTEM][A][B][E]
```

a new prompt ending at `[SYSTEM][A]` can reuse a checkpoint only if one was captured at or before that prefix. A later child cannot be "truncated" by slicing tensors: raw SWA rows are a logical ring and the compressor/indexer recurrent state is position-specific.

The reusable structure is nevertheless simple:

- compressed/indexer history is append-only;
- raw SWA, recurrent compressor/indexer state, counters, logits, and exact tokens form the terminal frontier;
- siblings share an immutable parent path;
- restore walks exactly one root-to-leaf chain.

No sibling merge or arbitrary substring reuse is causally valid. A tree therefore supplies the needed sharing without DAG machinery.

## Evidence and remaining unknown

Local M2 Ultra measurements with the 262,144-context MXFP4 Flash model found:

| State | Size | Synchronous time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Existing full KVC at ~2K | 49.93 MiB | median 56.3 ms |
| Existing full KVC at ~8K | 130.62 MiB | median 135.1 ms |
| Existing full KVC at ~32K | 453.35 MiB | median 468.0 ms |
| Exact terminal frontier, warm RAM | 22.88 MiB | p50 0.561 ms, p95 0.639 ms |
| Exact terminal frontier, first touch | 22.88 MiB | 2.7–4.3 ms |
| 23 MiB write plus `fsync` | 23 MiB | 5.1–6.3 ms |

At 2,048-token cadence, 128 conservative frontiers are about 2.86 GiB. Unique F32 compressed history is about 3.36 GiB, for roughly 6.22 GiB for one full 262K path. At the current natural 4,096-token Metal prefill cadence, frontier overhead is about 1.43 GiB.

These numbers justify an experiment. They do **not** measure the full node capture path. P0a must still prove that copying the unique compressed/indexer delta plus frontier regresses linear prefill by less than 5%.

## Goals

1. Restore the globally deepest compatible saved prefix no longer than the incoming prompt.
2. Share immutable compressed/indexer history across branches.
3. Preserve current rendered-text, exact-token, and BPE-safe suffix behavior.
4. Capture only states naturally reached by forward inference.
5. Bound RAM and disk independently and globally.
6. Keep inference locks off disk I/O.
7. Fail closed to an older node, KVC v1, or cold prefill.

## Non-goals

- arbitrary substring or infix reuse;
- synthesizing an earlier compressor frontier from a later state;
- a generic DAG, radix-tree database, pack/compaction layer, journal, or external dependency;
- changing tokenizer, request rendering, API endpoint semantics, DSpark/MTP policy, or resident-session scheduling;
- protocol aliases/trailers in P0;
- CPU, GLM, tensor-parallel, or distributed restore in P0;
- replacing KVC v1 before parity is demonstrated.

## Current behavior that remains authoritative

The high-level order remains:

1. specialized Responses/Anthropic/thinking live continuation;
2. live exact-token reuse or supported live rewind;
3. live rendered-byte prefix reuse;
4. durable cache candidates;
5. cold prefill.

Revision 4 changes step 4: tree metadata and KVC v1 metadata are queried together, and the server chooses the **globally deepest compatible prefix before loading a payload**. It must not choose a shallower tree node merely because tree lookup ran first.

At equal prefix depth:

1. prefer an already resident RAM tree node;
2. otherwise prefer the candidate with lower estimated restore cost;
3. use a deterministic final tie-breaker.

Unsupported protocol state remains tree-ineligible and follows the current KVC/live/cold path.

## Text match, token match, and node identity

Three concepts must remain separate.

### 1. `prefix_key`: lookup alias, not node identity

`prefix_key` is derived from the rendered prefix bytes and byte length using the existing hash scheme. It points to **one or more candidates**.

The mapping must be a multimap because equal rendered bytes can arise with different exact tokenizations, compatibility settings, or payloads. Every candidate is verified against actual rendered bytes before restore; hash equality alone is never a hit.

### 2. `node_id`: immutable state identity

A node ID identifies one exact cached state, for example from:

```text
cache_compat_id
+ parent_node_id
+ exact_token_delta
+ payload_digest
```

`parent_node_id`, never `prefix_key`, defines topology.

### 3. Exact tokens plus rendered suffix

After selecting a candidate:

1. reconstruct the exact cached token IDs from root-to-node token deltas;
2. verify the rendered byte prefix;
3. tokenize only the incoming rend

records.title: Proposal: RBAC enablement and write-governance rollout
records.body:
## Current state

DJ already has a working RBAC engine, wired into the request path and switched on in config. The default policy is `permissive`, so it allows everything today. The work below turns it into enforced write-governance, one namespace at a time.

### What exists today

- The data model: `roles`, `role_scopes`, and `role_assignments` tables. Principals are rows in `users` tagged by `kind` (user, service account, group).
- Five actions (read, write, execute, delete, manage) with a hierarchy and node/namespace scopes matched by cascading wildcard.
- Resolution that folds in group membership and skips expired assignments, behind pluggable group-membership and authorization services.
- An `AccessChecker` that endpoints call to register a request and check it.
- Service accounts, role/scope/assignment and group APIs, History events, and soft-delete on roles.
- [#2230](https://github.com/DataJunction/dj/pull/2230) merged: `MANAGE` checks on role/group administration.
- [#2232](https://github.com/DataJunction/dj/pull/2232) merged: admin break-glass bypass.

### What doesn't exist yet

Each gap notes the sequence step that closes it.

- Any actual denial. With `permissive` defaults a missing grant still allows the action, and there is no per-namespace, per-action restrictive scoping in production yet. (steps 4 and 7)
- Fail-closed grant delegation. #2230 adds `MANAGE` checks, but the permissive fallback can still allow a broad symbolic scope such as `node:*`, which can then override a governed namespace. (steps 0 and 1)
- Auto-ownership on create. Creating a node or namespace assigns no role. `node_owners` is display metadata the RBAC service never reads. (step 5)
- Full enforcement coverage. Some mutating endpoints never call `check()`, use the wrong action/resource, or mutate through deployment/background paths. (step 0)
- An ownership backfill from current owners. (step 6)
- A management UI for roles, scopes, assignments, or groups. (not in the MVP)
- Read and execute gating. (not in the MVP)

The sequence below is the plan to turn it on safely.

---

### Problem - metadata and ownership governance

Right now anyone can edit or delete anyone else's nodes, and nothing marks who owns a production node. Confidentiality is already handled downstream, so this is about protecting node definitions and giving them owners. Reads and queries stay as they are. The query engine still governs data access.

The plan is to enforce write/delete/manage first, leave read/execute permissive, and turn governance on one namespace at a time. A request is only protected if every path to the mutation performs a correct authorization check.

### How a request is decided

Owning a namespace is a role. Creating or provisioning a namespace gives its owner principal a role with `MANAGE` on the namespace boundary.

RBAC/group administration is fail-closed:

- admins are allowed through the logged break-glass path
- otherwise the caller needs an explicit `MANAGE` grant containing every scope they create, assign, change, or revoke
- permissive fallback and the default-access role cannot authorize grant administration

For an ordinary metadata request:

- admins are allowed, and the bypass is logged
- an explicit principal/group/service-account grant allows it
- with no explicit grant, a matching restrictive scope denies it
- with no restrictive match, the default-access role can grant fallback access
- with no fallback grant, the permissive default allows it

Reads and queries stay permissive. For the MVP, restrictive scopes remain config-backed via `RESTRICTIVE_SCOPES`. A DB-backed registry can follow if self-service governance is needed.

### Sequence

0. ![status: merged](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-merged-8250df?style=flat-square) **[#2334: Enforce access checks on mutating routes + add coverage guard](https://github.com/DataJunction/dj/pull/2334)** (HTTP coverage baseline merged; non-HTTP follow-ups block step 7).
   - Make RBAC/group administration require explicit `MANAGE`; never use permissive fallback.
   - Require delegated scopes to be contained by the caller's `MANAGE` scopes.
   - Audit roles and assignments created while administration was permissive, especially global and ancestor grants.
   - Check namespace create/reactivate and require `MANAGE` for Git configuration and owner changes.
   - Fix `remove_complex_dimension_link`, materialization, preagg, and cube writes.
   - Fix action/resource mismatches such as namespace deletion using `WRITE` and node copy checking the full node name as a namespace.
   - Use a route inventory test as a baseline, and carry authorization through deployment and background mutation paths.

1. ![status: merged](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-merged-8250df?style=flat-square) **[#2230: Enforce `MANAGE` on role/group admin APIs](https://github.com/DataJunction/dj/pull/2230)**.
   - The endpoint checks are merged.
   - ![status: merged](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-merged-8250df?style=flat-square) **[#2339: RBAC PR 1 follow-up: Fail closed for grant delegation](https://github.com/DataJunction/dj/pull/2339)**. Makes the control-plane path fail-closed and adds scope-containment checks for `node:*`, `namespace:*`, and malformed broad patterns.

2. ![status: merged](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-merged-8250df?style=flat-square) **[#2232: Admin break-glass bypass](https://github.com/DataJunction/dj/pull/2232)**.
   - The bypass is merged.

Seeds and verifies an admin before enforcement, and logs bypass use distinctly from ordinary grants.

records.title: Impact analysis overlay on the canvas
records.body:
#1724 added a dependents tab on the entity detail page. This is the equivalent on the canvas: select a node and see impact visually in the context of the diagram.

- **Overlay mode** — select one or more nodes and highlight everything transitively upstream and/or downstream via connected edges, dimming the rest of the diagram.
- **Direction and depth** — toggle dependents vs. dependencies, and limit traversal depth.
- **Model-aware** — for entity-linked shapes, optionally traverse catalog relations rather than just drawn edges, surfacing impact that isn't visible in this particular diagram.
- **Cycle detection** — highlight dependency cycles as a secondary mode.

The graph package should already provide the traversal primitives. Related to #1724.

records.title: Handle inverse and sub-properties (normalize inverses at ingest, expand sub-properties at query time)
records.body:
## Summary

Design notes for handling **inverse properties** and **sub-properties** in GrEBI. These feel like one problem but want different solutions. Recommendation up front:

- **Inverse → ingest-time canonicalization** (normalize each inverse pair to one predicate + direction)
- **Sub-property → query-time type-union expansion** (expand a requested predicate to itself + its transitive sub-predicates)

Both share one new build artifact — a **predicate-metadata table** (sub-property closure + inverse pairs) — which can be derived from the ontology datasource added in #47.

## Two different problems

**Inverse properties** — e.g. `biolink:has_phenotype` ⇄ `biolink:phenotype_of`. Different sources assert different directions of the same fact. This is a *normalization* problem: we want one canonical way to express each relationship.

**Sub-properties** — `rdfs:subPropertyOf` chains, e.g. `biolink:causes` ⊑ `biolink:contributes_to` ⊑ `biolink:related_to`. A query for the general predicate should also match the specific ones. This is a *closure/expansion* problem, structurally identical to the subclass `redundant`/`nonredundant` trick in #47.

## Current state

- Edges become Neo4j relationship types verbatim — `grebi_make_neo_csv` (`dataload/06_create_neo_db/grebi_make_neo_csv/src/main.rs`) writes `edge.edge_type` straight into the `:TYPE` column.
- Query templates hard-code single predicates, e.g. `-[:`biolink:related_to`]->` in `query_templates/hello_world.yaml`.
- The only predicate normalization today is `additional_equivalence_groups` in `configs/subgraph_configs/src/shared.py`, which merges *synonymous* predicates (e.g. `ols:directParent` = `rdfs:subClassOf`) but does **not** handle property hierarchy or inverses.

## The big lever from #47

PR #47 ingests Ubergraph/ontologies as data, so **the property hierarchy and inverse axioms are now in the graph as facts** — `rdfs:subPropertyOf` and `owl:inverseOf` edges between predicate entities. We don't need to hardcode a mapping from the Biolink YAML; we can *derive* the predicate-metadata table from the ontology datasource itself, the same source of truth the rest of the pipeline already trusts. This is the foundation for both halves below.

## Inverse: normalize at ingest, not query time

For inverses, query-time is the wrong place — if both directions stay live, every query must consider both forever. Instead, canonicalize each inverse pair to **one predicate + one direction** during ingest (a cheap relabel in `grebi_link` or earlier — no graph growth). Pick the canonical member from the inverse-pair table.

Caveat: if a source genuinely asserts both directions as distinct provenance, canonicalizing merges them — but edges already carry `grebi:datasources` as a **set**, so the merge is lossless for provenance.

## Sub-properties: expand at query time

Query-time is the right call here, and the contrast with subclass is instructive. Subclass closure is *materialized* (redundant graph) because nodes are queried by hierarchy constantly. Property closure materialized as duplicate edges would multiply **edge** count by predicate-tree depth × every source — expensive and baked-in at load.

Instead, expand the predicate at query-build time. Neo4j matches a union of relationship types efficiently via the rel-type index:

```cypher
// query asks for related_to; expand to its sub-property descendants
MATCH (gene)-[assoc:`biolink:related_to`|`biolink:causes`|`biolink:contributes_to`|...]->(disease)
```

Mechanically:
1. At ingest, walk `rdfs:subPropertyOf` edges from the ontology datasource and precompute a **closure table**: predicate → all transitive sub-predicates. It's tiny (hundreds of entries) — load it into the API like the existing `PrefixService`/prefix map, **not** into Neo4j.
2. In `GrebiCypherRepo` (`webapp/grebi_api/.../repo/GrebiCypherRepo.java`), expand each predicate in the Cypher fragment to the `|`-union of itself + descendants before sending to the cypher service.

**The trap:** very general predicates (`biolink:related_to`) can expand to hundreds of types and the union scan gets slow. Mitigations, in order of effort: cap expansion depth; let a query template opt out of expansion per-predicate; or materialize closure edges *only* for the handful of hot general predicates (hybrid) while expanding everything else at query time.

## Alternative worth knowing about

Instead of type-union, store predicate ancestors as a relationship property and filter:

```cypher
MATCH (a)-[r]->(b) WHERE 'biolink:related_to' IN r.`grebi:predicateAncestors`
```

Simpler to generate, but abandons the rel-type index and scans — slower at scale. Only worth reaching for if type-union hits Neo4j limits on general predicates.

## Proposed plan

1. **Build the predicate-metadata table first** — extract sub-property closure + inverse pairs from the ontology datasource (#47). Shared foundation for both halves.
2. **Inverse → ingest-time canonicalization** in `grebi_link`, driven by `owl:inverseOf`.
3. **Sub-property → query-time type-union expansion** in `GrebiCypherRepo`, driven by the `rdfs:subPropertyOf` closure table, with a per-predicate opt-out and a depth cap for pathological general predicates.

## Open questions

- Sub-property expansion **on by default** for all templates, or opt-in per predicate? Default-on is more useful but risks the general-predicate slowdown.
- Should canonicalizing inverses be allowed to **merge** two edges into one (collapsing provenance into the datasources set), or must they stay distinct edges?
